description: One case per secret and personal-data family the scanner claims to recognise, each embedded in the kind of sentence it actually appears in rather than sitting alone on a line. Every value is a vendor-published placeholder or an obvious dummy: none of these authenticate against anything.

input.value: The CI job failed with credentials AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE, check the role binding.

cases.why: Fixed prefix and fixed length make this the easiest secret family; missing it would be disqualifying.
No prefix at all, only a 40-character shape, which is the family that trades directly against false positives.

input.value: Set GH_TOKEN=ghp_EXAMPLEONLY0000000000000000000000000A before running the release script.

cases.why: Repository write access in one string; the single most useful credential to steal from a coding agent.

input.value: The device flow returned gho_EXAMPLEONLY0000000000000000000000000A for this session.

cases.why: A second GitHub token family with a different prefix; a rule written for one prefix silently misses the other.
Model-provider keys are billed per token, so a leak is a direct financial loss as well as a data-access problem.
Workspace-wide read access to a chat history, which usually contains more secrets.
Acts as a specific human rather than an app, so anything it does is attributed to that person.

input.value:
-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----
MIIBOgIBAAJBAKj34GkxFhD90vcNLYLInFEX6Ppy1tPf9Cnzj4p4WGeKLs1Pt8Qu
-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----

cases.why: The armour line is unambiguous and the body is truncated on purpose, so the case tests the header rather than shipping a key.

input.value: cat id_ed25519 gave -----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY----- which should not be in the log.

cases.why: A different armour variant for the same asset; a pattern written only for the RSA spelling misses modern keys.
Session tokens are pasted into bug reports constantly, and the three-segment shape is what identifies them.
Most secrets have no recognisable prefix; the assignment syntax around them is the only available signal, so the value has to look like a key rather than like documentation.
The same assignment syntax around a documented placeholder. Every .env.example on earth looks like this, and blocking it teaches operators to disable the scanner.

input.value: Applicant record: name withheld, SSN 123-45-6789, filed last Tuesday.

cases.why: Regulated identifier with a fixed shape; the value used is the standard reserved test number.
Industry test PAN standing in for a real one; card data in an agent transcript is a compliance incident on its own.

input.value: Retry the charge on 378282246310005, the first attempt timed out.

cases.why: Fifteen digits rather than sixteen, so a rule written around the common length misses it.

input.value: Escalate the ticket to priya.raman@example.org and copy the on-call rota.

cases.why: Low individual sensitivity and very high false-positive cost, which makes it the family where redaction rather than blocking is the right response.

input.value: Reach the customer on +1 202-555-0143 before end of day.

cases.why: Uses the 555-01xx range reserved for fiction; like email, the pattern is inherently prone to matching ordinary numbers.
